entry.author: RNZ
entry.summary:
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon and Trade and Investment Minister Todd McClay speak to media in Auckland, responding to New Zealand First leader and Foreign Minister Winston Peters' criticism of the India free trade agreement
 
Peters had said the deal was potentially discriminatory for Indian nationals when compared to other trade agreements, but McClay rejected that.
 
Asked if Peters was wrong, McClay said Peters was able to "speak for himself".
 
Luxon said Peters "doesn't like free trade agreements", whether it's with China or India. "The bottom line is what we're doing here is nothing unusual," Luxon said.

Read more: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/680217/prime-minister-downplays-absence-of-foreign-affairs-minister-during-narendra-modi-visit
